en: The graduate school's call page for the joint degree doctoral programmes (国際連携総合医学専攻). It gives the application period of each call and links the application guidelines (PDF), the sets of forms (ZIP) and the form for the eligibility pre-screening (事前資格審査). Lund applicants also need Lund's own application form.

en: How companies set up joint research with Nagoya University researchers. After consulting the faculty member who will lead the research, send the application (共同研究申請書) and a draft contract as electronic files to the Research Support Section (経営企画課研究支援係). Clinical research needs the approval of the university's ethics committee first. The page also sets the indirect costs (30%) and the fee for company researchers who work on site.

en: The faculty's page on gifts to Nagoya University from companies, organisations and individuals. To give, send the donation application form (寄附申込書, Form 1) to the Research Support Section of the Management Planning Division (経営企画課研究支援係). Once the gift is accepted, you receive a payment request, then a receipt about a month after payment. A set share of each gift pays for administration.

en: Instructions for students and graduates seeking a US medical license. For a USMLE status verification, email the Graduate Section of the Student Affairs Division (学務課大学院係); the address is on the page. For an MSPE, apply and pay online, then email a draft with evidence. The last date is the end of May of that year (当年５月末日), and issuing takes at least one month.

en: The faculty's page for the press. To interview or film faculty members, apply with the online press and filming request form (報道取材・撮影許可願). The page also offers a Word template of the letter asking for a staff member's outside work (兼業依頼状). The General Affairs Section of the General Affairs Division (総務課 総務係) handles requests.

en: A page on the Office of International Affairs' own exchange site, with two topics. It introduces the Frontier Association (フロンティア会), an alumni group run by students who trained abroad, founded in 1998; its representative teaches students preparing to go abroad how to examine patients and write records in English. It also explains how to request a courtesy visit and lists past visits.
